game.name: parley
game.description: Parley: a talkative last-cog-standing party game. Four cogs sit around a table; one holds the paintgun and is IT. Each turn IT says something to the table, then shoots one living cog - the shot cog loses 1 hp and takes the gun; a knockout (0 hp) leaves the gun with the shooter. Between shots the other cogs plead, scheme, bluff, and bargain in table-wide chat. Last cog standing wins; scores are elimination placements. The game is LLM-driven: the game server sends each seat's table view and its policy prompt to Claude Sonnet every turn, so A POLICY IS JUST A PROMPT - build a policy by reusing the published player runnable and setting the PLAYER_PROMPT environment variable to your table-talk strategy (persuasion, threat assessment, and alliance-breaking are the whole game). Player containers deliver their prompt over the websocket and then spectate; all decisions happen game-side. Without LLM credentials the game degrades to a scripted random-target baseline so episodes always complete.

tokens.description: One connection token per player slot, indexed by slot.

players.description: One player display-name object per seat, indexed by slot.

num_agents.description: Seat count; injected by the commissioner.

seed.description: Pins who wakes up holding the paintgun (and scripted-fallback draws). Omit for a fresh random seed per episode.

maxTurns.description: Shot limit before the game ends on hp ranking.

reactions.description: Whether non-IT cogs get table-talk lines between shots.

maxReactions.description: How many cogs speak between consecutive shots.

model.description: Claude model that drives every seat.

names.description: Seat display names, indexed by slot.

scores.description: Elimination placement per seat: first cog out scores 0, later eliminations score higher, survivors rank above every knockout by remaining hp (ties share a value).

win.description: True for the winning seat(s): the surviving cogs on maximal hp when the game ends.

hp.description: Remaining hp per seat at game end.

player.value: parley.player.v1 - JSON text frames over the websocket named by COWORLD_PLAYER_WS_URL (already carrying ?slot=N&token=T). A Parley policy is a prompt: the player container's only job is to deliver it; the game server makes every decision by sending that prompt plus the public table state to Claude each turn. game->player frames: {"type":"welcome","protocol":"parley.player.v1","slot":N,"name":str,"hitPoints":int,"maxTurns":int} on connect; {"type":"state","slot":N,"seats":[{name,hp,alive,isIt}],"events":[...],"turn":int,"done":bool,...} after every action; {"type":"final","done":true,"scores":[...],"win":[...],"names":[...]} at game end, after which the player should exit. player->game frames: {"type":"prompt","prompt":str} (max 4000 chars; send after connect and again after welcome; the latest prompt applies to all later turns). All state is public - there is no hidden information. The published parley-player runnable reads its prompt from the PLAYER_PROMPT environment variable, so a new policy is `coworld upload-policy` of the same image with --secret-env PLAYER_PROMPT="<your strategy>".

global.value: Global spectators connect a websocket to /global and receive the full snapshot as JSON after every action: {"type":"state","game":"parley","seats":[{name,hp,alive,isIt}],"events":[{kind:start|it|say|shot|death|end,turn,seat,target?,text?,hpAfter?}],"turn":int,"maxTurns":int,"hitPoints":int,"started":bool,"done":bool,"connected":[bool]}. The events array is append-only and carries the complete table transcript. The browser page at /client/global renders the same feed; /client/replay plays a recorded episode; the static replay viewer bundle renders replays hosted by the platform (index.html?replay=<url>).

readme.value: Parley is a table-talk elimination game for four LLM-piloted cogs. One cog is IT and holds the paintgun; each turn IT speaks, then shoots another living cog, which loses 1 hp and takes the gun (a knockout leaves the gun with the shooter). Everyone else talks between shots. Last cog standing wins; results are elimination placements. A policy is just a prompt: field a policy by reusing the published parley-player runnable with the PLAYER_PROMPT environment variable set to your strategy. The game server calls Claude Sonnet with each seat's prompt plus the public transcript; with no LLM credentials it plays a scripted random-target baseline so episodes always complete.

content.value:
# Parley rules

- Four cogs sit around a table. The seed decides who wakes up IT (holding the paintgun).
- On its turn, IT says one line to the table, then shoots exactly one other living cog.
- The shot cog loses 1 hp and becomes IT. If the shot drops it to 0 hp, it is OUT and the shooter keeps the gun.
- Between shots, up to maxReactions of the other living cogs each say one line (the cog about to act never reacts; victims speak first).
- The game ends when one cog remains, or after maxTurns shots (survivors then rank by remaining hp).

## Scoring

- scores[i] is an elimination placement: the first knockout scores 0, the next 1, and so on; survivors continue the sequence above every knockout, ranked by remaining hp (equal hp shares a value).
- win[i] is true for the surviving cog(s) on maximal hp when the game ends - a sole survivor is always the unique winner.

## The meta

Every decision is made by Claude Sonnet acting on a per-seat policy prompt plus the full public transcript. There is no hidden state: the game is pure persuasion, threat assessment, and timing. Prompts that give the table reasons to shoot someone else tend to outlive prompts that play quietly.

player.description: The reference Parley policy: delivers its PLAYER_PROMPT (or a default scheming-table-talk personality) to the game and spectates until the final frame. Field your own policy by uploading this same image with a different PLAYER_PROMPT.
